messages.subject: Difficulty specifying multidimensional model correctly
parts:
Dear Phil,

sorry for asking a question that I should be able to answer myself. I tried, but am clueless so far.

I am conducting an analysis of factorial validity and compare multidimensional models to the unidimensional model (confirmatory analysis). While my unidimensional model results in LL = -10439.28, some of the multidimensional models result in higher (!) LL. Consider the following model specifications:
  • unidimensional:

M0 <- '
FK = 1-27
COV = FK*FK
'
model.mirt.M0 <- mirt.model(M0)
fit.mirt.M0.1PL <- mirt(dat,model.mirt.M0,itemtype='Rasch')

  • multidimensional:
M1 <- '
fpw = 2,4,5,7,9,11,12,26,27
qn = 3,6,8,10,13,14,17,21,22
ql = 1,15,16,18,19,20,23,24,25
COV = fpw*qn*ql
'
model.mirt.M1 <- mirt.model(M1)
fit.mirt.M1.1PL <- mirt(dat,model.mirt.M1,itemtype='Rasch')

The multidimensional model results in LL=-10449.122, which is higher than regarding model M0. This should not happen as the models are nested and model M1 estimates more parameters.

Doing the same analyses with Conquest results in different LL (smaller, making more sense) than with the mirt-package. I guess that something is wrong with the model specification. I already tried freeing the means, stating the COV differently, defining constraints, etc. All resulting in the exact same LL.

I'd appreciate any kind of hint ...

Thanks so much, best wishes
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Difficulty specifying multidimensional model correctly
parts:
It's possibly related to the reduced number of integration nodes for higher dimensions, though the dev version now uses a few more for a 3 factor model (15 versus the previous 11). I'm going to release the next version of mirt shortly, so try again after updating to version 1.10 (or just install it from Github manually). 

This is what I get for a comparable situation:

data <- key2binary(SAT12,
                   key = c(1,4,5,2,3,1,2,1,3,1,2,4,2,1,5,3,4,4,1,4,3,3,4,1,3,5,1,3,1,5,4,5))
dat <- data[,1:27]

> anova(fit.mirt.M1.1PL, fit.mirt.M0.1PL)

Model 1: mirt(data = dat, model = model.mirt.M0, itemtype = "Rasch")
Model 2: mirt(data = dat, model = model.mirt.M1, itemtype = "Rasch")

       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik    X2  df      p
1 16057.36 16060.21 16091.58 16180.48 -8000.681   NaN NaN    NaN
2 16066.80 16070.76 16107.13 16211.89 -8000.398 0.566   5 0.9895

messages.author: 3244ec4c6037ea07
messages.subject: Re: Difficulty specifying multidimensional model correctly
parts:
Dear all,

this topic was continued in private discussion. Phil found out that the traits/factors are very highly correlated and thus the algorithm was stuck in a local minimum. It helped a great deal using method="MHRM" instead of EM. Also changing the starting values of the factor correlations helped (by default .25, changed to .75).

Quick summary: when a multidimensional model results in higher absolute LL than the unidimensional model ...
  • update mirt to newest version
  • change starting values
  • use different method, especially MH-RM

Best of luck to everyone and special thanks to Phil who spent his leisure time to help!

Chris
